reported_mineral_classes.evidence: Opportunity examined Burns formation outcrops on Victoria crater's northwestern side. Arvidson et al. (2015) report that their Mossbauer spectra indicate hematite among the Fe-bearing phases. Hematite-rich spherules/concretions occur in the crater's sulfate-rich sedimentary rocks.
reported_mineral_classes.instrument: Opportunity rover Mossbauer spectrometer; supporting rover imaging

reported_mineral_classes.evidence: Arvidson et al. (2015) explicitly identify jarosite among the Fe-rich phases indicated by Opportunity Mossbauer observations of Burns formation outcrops on Victoria crater's northwestern side. This is evidence of an acid-sulfate alteration mineral, but gives no 5 km abundance or area fraction.

Arvidson et al. (2015) list minor pyroxene among the iron-bearing phases indicated by Opportunity Mossbauer measurements of Victoria crater northwestern Burns formation outcrops. The cited data do not specify its area fraction or a site-wide concentration.

Arvidson et al. (2015) interpret CRISM FRT0001C7D2 observations of wind-scoured bedrock on Victoria crater's southeastern rim/wall (near Explorer crater) as kieserite-bearing material. A ~2.129 micrometre absorption is consistent with kieserite, but features are shallow/noisy; the rover did not examine this southeastern exposure in situ.

reported_lithology_classes.evidence: Opportunity studied an approximately 8 m vertical section of sulfate-rich Burns formation sandstone on Victoria crater walls. Sulfate enrichment describes the rock material; it is not a mineral-specific mapped percent.

regional_context_minerals_not_site_confi.evidence: Olivine occurs in basaltic soils across Meridiani Planum, but this cited regional evidence does not establish an olivine occurrence in the exact Victoria footprint. It should not be counted as a locally confirmed class.

published_observations.location_description: Burns formation exposed in the northwestern wall and outcrops of Victoria crater, surveyed by Opportunity
published_observations.interpretation: Rover data indicate hematite, jarosite, minor pyroxene, and an unidentified Fe(III) phase; this is a point/outcrop-scale mineral observation, not an area map.

published_observations.location_description: Wind-scoured southeastern Victoria crater rim/wall near Explorer crater
published_observations.interpretation: CRISM ~2.129 um absorption is interpreted as kieserite; a ~1.94 um feature suggests an additional unresolved hydrated phase. These are spectral inferences, not in-situ identifications or abundance maps.

spectral_caveats.interpretation: Arvidson et al. (2015) report pervasive gypsum signature at Botany Bay in Endeavour crater, NOT at Victoria. Do not transfer that detection to Victoria.
An approximately 1.94 um absorption at southeastern Victoria indicates hydration but is insufficient to identify a unique mineral species.

methods.area: No georeferenced mineral polygons or mineral abundance rasters were intersected with the 5 km footprint. mapped_fraction=0 indicates no mineral map coverage, NOT absence of the minerals.
methods.literature_extraction: Mineral classes are taken from published Victoria-crater-specific Opportunity measurements and CRISM spectra. Rover-measured phases are distinguished from orbital mineral inferences and Meridiani-wide context.
methods.location_test: Victoria crater is at the fixed -2.05 N, 354.5 E analysis center; its ~0.8 km rim/walls and Opportunity investigation are within the nominal 5 km square. Localities are crater-associated, but no individual measurement coordinate or map polygon was overlaid on the square.
methods.caveat: Presence in individual crater outcrops does not imply uniform occurrence throughout the 5 km region. Do not infer mineral concentrations, area percentages, or generalized Mars-Earth similarity from these observations. Kieserite remains a spectral interpretation.
methods.stage2_scoring: Context only. Do not calculate Earth-Mars mineral-similarity scores from this qualitative profile; wait for compatible Earth and Mars spatial mineral maps.
